comments.body:
Fixed by #798 (merged, `94c68c20c4`).

The cause wasn't specific to child agents: #740's check read `sleep` (so `sleep 60; echo finished > ks-child.txt` and `sleep 60`) and every `sed` without `-i` as "may hide a write", so Grant once stayed offered. Now `sleep`, `date`, `seq`, `expr`, `nproc` and `uptime` count as writing nothing, and so does a `sed` whose scripts only select, print, delete, list, count or quit lines (no `-i`/`-f`/`-l`, nothing a shell may expand). Anything the text can't show still keeps the offer. A real child agent's prompt is covered by a test (fails before, passes after, on macOS and Linux).

Replay of AGG-R14 (GLM 5.3 Flash, disposable home): the child's prompt now says "Grant once is not offered for this command: …" with no Grant once option. [Video](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-789-issue789-child-no-useless-grant-576ea39ea970-2026-10-14.mp4); screens in `qa/security-levels/fixes/issue-789-20261014/`.

What runs and what is denied are unchanged; Permissive and Moderate are untouched.

title: Aggressive: Grant once still offered on child-agent prompts (and after a spawn) where it cannot apply (#740 follow-up)
